one_liner: Header-only C++17/20 dynamic bitset beating std::vector<bool> on word-level shift/count operations in third-party benchmarks.
what_it_does: A resizable-at-runtime bit container closer in spirit to boost::dynamic_bitset than to std::bitset: block-based storage (default block type uint64_t) with set/reset/flip/count/shift/find operations and operator&, |, ^, ~, ==, comparisons. It is not a literal drop-in replacement for std::vector<bool>: it is a distinct template class (sul::dynamic_bitset<Block>), exposes no standard iterators (bit access goes through a reference-proxy object, same limitation as std::vector<bool>), and treats equality/comparison as size-sensitive rather than numeric.
how_it_is_fast: Operations work a whole block (64 bits by default) at a time over an internal std::vector<Block>, instead of the per-bit iteration generic std:: algorithms perform on std::vector<bool>'s bit-reference proxy. Shifts, fills, and transforms move/OR/AND whole words; population count uses compiler builtins or C++20 <bit> intrinsics, and can optionally call kimwalisch/libpopcnt (SIMD popcount) if its header is found at compile time.
when_to_use: Large bit vectors (roughly 10^5+ bits) doing frequent shift_left/shift_right, count, fill, or transform, where std::vector<bool>'s per-bit loop dominates runtime
Want boost::dynamic_bitset-like ergonomics (resizable size, bitwise operators, find-next) without taking a Boost dependency
Bitset size is only known at runtime, ruling out std::bitset<N>
Want an optional SIMD-accelerated popcount (via libpopcnt) for hot counting loops without writing it yourself
Want a single header you can vendor into a codebase with no build step
when_not_to_use: Small bitsets (<=256 bits) doing fill/set-style operations: the measured win over std::vector<bool> is marginal (~1.9x) or a loss (large-size fill is ~1.2x SLOWER, large set is roughly tied)
Code needs std::bitset's fixed compile-time size, constexpr-friendliness, or std::vector<bool>'s standard iterator/algorithm compatibility
Code performs bitwise ops (&, |, ^, comparisons) on operands of different sizes expecting boost-style zero-padding: the maintainer explicitly rejected that semantics (see gotchas)
Need boost::dynamic_bitset's full feature surface (this library states a narrower one)

Want first-party, reproducible performance numbers before committing: the cited results are from a third-party (BitLib) README, not dynamic_bitset's own benchmark repo, and no compiler, flags, or CPU model are given

integration.dependencies: none required; optional kimwalisch/libpopcnt (auto-detected via __has_include, used for faster count() if present and not disabled with DYNAMIC_BITSET_NO_LIBPOPCNT)
integration.min_toolchain: C++17 (C++20 optional, enables <bit> intrinsics); CMake 3.10+ only needed if consumed as a CMake subproject
integration.platforms: any (CI covers Ubuntu, Windows MSVC, Windows MSYS2, macOS); no SIMD/ISA requirement for the library itself, only for the optional libpopcnt dependency
integration.thread_safety: not documented; treat as an ordinary unsynchronized container, same as std::vector<bool>
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — explain: API resembles std::vector<bool>/boost::dynamic_bitset (resize, push_back, operator[], bitwise ops) but it's a different type, has no standard iterators, and comparisons are size-sensitive rather than numeric, so call sites need adaptation, not a type swap

gotchas: operator&, |, ^, ==, and comparisons all require the caller to manage sizes; the maintainer explicitly rejected boost-style 'pad the shorter operand with zeros' semantics (issue #4) because it breaks algebraic properties like (a^b^b)==a, so mixed-size use needs care
No standard iterators: bit access uses a reference-proxy object (like std::vector<bool>), so range-for/std::algorithm code expecting real iterators won't compile

libpopcnt use is silent and header-detected at compile time; vendoring only dynamic_bitset.hpp without libpopcnt.h means count() falls back to builtin popcount, so the cited count() benchmark numbers may not reproduce as-is

As of the versions discussed in issue #9, there was no documented to_ulong()/to_ullong()-style conversion beyond unsigned long long width without asserts/UB — check the current header if you need numeric conversion
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick this over BitLib when you want an in-place, resizable container with boost::dynamic_bitset-style ergonomics rather than a span/iterator-based bit-algorithms library (BitLib actually posted faster shift_left/reverse numbers on the same large-size benchmark). Pick over plf::bitset when the size is only known at runtime, not compile-time. CRoaring and pasta::bit_vector target compressed/succinct/rank-select workloads, not general mutable dense bitsets, so they answer a different problem than dynamic_bitset.
verified_claims_summary: On BitLib's (bkille/BitLib) third-party Google Benchmark suite — not dynamic_bitset's own repo — sul::dynamic_bitset beat std::vector<bool> by ~26x (small) to ~165x (16,777,216-bit) on shift_left and ~37x to ~161x on count; it was ~1.9x faster than std:: on small fill but ~1.2x slower on large fill (429,375 ns vs 356,517 ns), with large-size set roughly tied (2.37 ns vs 2.39 ns). No compiler, compiler flags, or CPU model are stated on the benchmark page.
status_note: Actively maintained (last commit 2026-09-12, MIT license) by a single maintainer who has said free time is limited; being a small header-only file, it's easy to vendor and keep working even if upstream slows further.
